title: Hunter-gatherers built Gobekli Tepe's carved stone enclosures
body: In what is now south-eastern Turkey, people erected monumental enclosures from about 9,600 to 8,200 BCE. Their T-shaped stone pillars carry carvings of wild animals.
takeaway: The site shows that people gathered and organised large building projects very early in the region's settled history.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Gobekli Tepe (2018)
visual: tall T-shaped stone pillars rising inside a shallow circular enclosure

title: One Uruguayan factory landscape traces the trade in preserved meat
body: At Fray Bentos, a factory founded in 1859 processed cattle from Uruguay's prairies. Meat extract and corned beef went to European buyers from 1865, and frozen meat was exported from 1924.
takeaway: Changing how food was preserved widened the choice of goods a distant factory could sell.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Fray Bentos Industrial Landscape (2015)
